title: The Agency Service Fee on Air Ticket Fare Brands Bookings
content:
The agency service fee is the charge the agency makes for its own work on an Air Ticket Fare Brands booking, as distinct from anything the airline charges. Its rate is scheduled brand by brand.

## 1. The condition in force

The service fee is not refunded when the traveller later cancels, because the service it pays for has already been performed; it is refunded in full only where the agency itself cancelled the itinerary in error.

Two consequences follow from that single clause and nothing else. A cancellation by the traveller, at whatever point and on whatever brand, leaves the service fee where it stands. A cancellation the agency itself made in error returns the fee in full, and not in part.

| Who cancelled | Reason | What becomes of the service fee |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the traveller | any | not refunded |
| the agency | its own error | refunded in full |

## 2. Clauses no longer in force

> "The agency service fee is charged once per traveller on the booking at the moment the ticket is issued, and is stated separately from the airline fare and from taxes and carrier fees."

That clause is **no longer in force**. The handling basis it stated has been superseded by the basis now governing the agency service charge on Air Ticket Fare Brands bookings. The brand values scheduled under this policy are unaffected and stand as stated.

> "The fee follows the fare brand held, not the cabin flown, so a business cabin sold under a saver brand carries the saver brand's fee."

That clause is **no longer in force**. The handling basis it stated has been superseded by the basis now governing the agency service charge on Air Ticket Fare Brands bookings. The brand values scheduled under this policy are unaffected and stand as stated.

> "Where the traveller elects to be charged in a currency other than the ticketing currency, the conversion markup of the fare brand held is added to the converted total, and the markup is disclosed before the card is taken."

That clause is **no longer in force**. The handling basis it stated has been superseded by the basis now governing the agency service charge on Air Ticket Fare Brands bookings. The brand values scheduled under this policy are unaffected and stand as stated.

The charging basis those three clauses carried — the fee taken once per traveller at the moment of ticketing, at the rate of the brand held, with the brand's conversion markup added on a foreign-currency election — is retired with them. The rates themselves are unaffected: the scheduled agency service fee and conversion markup of each brand remain the brand's own values.

## 3. Point of judgement

**Does the retirement of the charging clauses touch the refund clause?** It does not. Only the named clauses are retired; the condition in section 1 governing what becomes of the fee on a cancellation stands as it is written.

superseded_clauses: The agency service fee is charged once per traveller on the booking at the moment the ticket is issued, and is stated separately from the airline fare and from taxes and carrier fees.
The fee follows the fare brand held, not the cabin flown, so a business cabin sold under a saver brand carries the saver brand's fee.

Where the traveller elects to be charged in a currency other than the ticketing currency, the conversion markup of the fare brand held is added to the converted total, and the markup is disclosed before the card is taken.
